In California, a car must be smogged when you register or renew its registration, and also when you sell or transfer ownership of a vehicle that is more than four years old [d1][d7]. The California Smog Check Program requires vehicles manufactured in 1976 or later to undergo a biennial (every two years) smog inspection [d7][d3]. Vehicles more than eight model years old must be smog tested every two years, while gasoline-powered cars less than eight model years old are generally exempt from the biennial requirement [d6][d5]. When selling a car, the seller must provide a valid smog certificate if the vehicle is over four years old; if it is four years old or newer, the new owner pays a smog transfer fee instead of requiring an inspection [d1][d3]. Key exemptions include gasoline-powered vehicles that are 1975 model year or older, diesel vehicles manufactured before 1998 or weighing over 14,000 lbs, electric vehicles, trailers, and motorcycles [d7][d6][d2]. Additionally, smog inspections at registration renewal are only required if you live in one of the specified participating California counties (such as Los Angeles, San Francisco, Sacramento, and others) [d6].
